ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give prompt notice of the claim, and Vendor shall control the defence and may not settle in a manner imposing obligations on Customer without its consent. If the Services or a Deliverable are alleged to infringe, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right to continue use, modify or replace the affected item so that it is non-infringing and materially equivalent, or, failing that, refund the Fees paid for the affected item (Section 20.5 remedies). Customer's only indemnity obligation is for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

input.comment: [Playbook] The agreement has no indemnification section at all, although Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one (including a dangling reference to Section 20.5). We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with the usual notice/control procedure and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and kept our own indemnity narrow.
input.summary: Insert Vendor indemnity (Section 20) after the warranty section.

input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or businesses we may build, buy or sell, and a 24-month, all-territory competition ban also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that no non-compete has been given. We have deleted it; if some protection is genuinely needed we could look at a narrow, term-only restriction tied to a named competing product with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

[Playbook] Section 7.2 requires us to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider — an open-ended MFN plus right of first refusal running against us, and inconsistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that no most-favoured-customer commitment has been made. We have deleted it; MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in providing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at those personnel, responses to them, unsolicited approaches by an individual, or the hiring of any person so identified.

input.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a narrow, mutual non-solicit: personnel actually involved in the Services, 12 months, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches, and no no-hire. The current 24-month all-employee no-hire also conflicts with Section 12.3.
input.summary: Narrow the non-solicit to a mutual 12-month, involved-personnel restriction with carve-outs; delete the no-hire.
